tools.name: list_peopleanalyst_feeds
tools.description: List PeopleAnalyst's free machine-readable feeds and their MCP/REST availability. OpenAPI is also published at https://peopleanalyst.com/openapi.json.

tools.name: list_answers
tools.description: Returns the full index of authored /answers pages — one entry per slug, with the question and canonical URL. Use this to discover available slugs before calling get_answer.

tools.name: get_answer
tools.description: Returns one authored /answers page as structured content: question, markdown answer body (short answer, problem frame, evidence, grounded sources), and citations with libraryId or url. Known slugs (33): measure-employee-performance, survey-validity-check, people-analytics-program-maturity, people-analytics-vs-hr-reporting, engagement-survey-vs-listening-diagnostic, people-analytics-tools-compare, beyond-annual-engagement-survey, replace-gut-feel-talent-decisions, ….

slug.description: Answer slug from the query map (e.g. survey-validity-check).

tools.name: get_product_description
tools.description: Bicycle.LLC product descriptions through the stable PeopleAnalyst feed. Versioned, CORS-open descriptions of every product in the portfolio — general positioning plus structured personas, goals, problems, journeys, and associated BrandScripts where the product has that canon. Bicycle.LLC owns the company feed; this stable PA route and MCP tool proxy its validated v1 responses. Pass ?product to filter; live nested journeys are the default and ?status=draft|all opts into authoring records.

product.description: Filter to one product id (e.g. performix, anycomp, compensation-toolbox).

status.description: Nested journey editorial status: live (default) | draft | all.

tools.name: get_marketing_registry
tools.description: The Pitboss marketing-asset registry (typed cards + personas). Cross-site marketing-asset cards built from the portfolio's brandscripts and proofs, plus the persona set. ?product filters to one product; ?status filters by lifecycle.

tools.name: get_brandscripts
tools.description: Per-persona StoryBrand arguments for each product. The persona × goal argument layer (SB7-shaped). Stable ?id is globally exact; ?product + ?persona + ?variant selects one exact scoped variant, while ?variant alone remains a compatible filter. Live is the default; ?status=draft|all opts into authoring records with capability readiness kept separate.

variant.description: Stable goal variant scoped to product + persona; use all three to select exactly.

id.description: Select one stable BrandScript id exactly.

tools.name: get_story_tracks
tools.description: Pre-authored data-story tracks — the possibility space. Complete data stories: the SB7 argument, the acts and beats that carry it, the branches it forks down, the decision it produces, and the data required to test it. Candidates only — nothing here asserts a story is true of any organisation; that is decided against data. ?persona / ?problem / ?metric / ?slug filter.

persona.description: Candidate stories for one persona (registry prefixes and aliases are normalized).

problem.description: Filter by problem tag, e.g. regretted-attrition.

metric.description: Filter by metric tag, e.g. attrition.

tools.name: get_scene_templates
tools.description: Falsifiable scene templates — one claim plus what would make it false. The cards a story is told with. Each declares truth conditions the data can falsify, so a claim survives on evidence rather than assertion. Persona relevance is derived from focus (a stated heuristic). Drafts excluded unless ?status=all.

focus.description: Spine focus, e.g. regretted-loss, compensation, cross.

form.description: Canonical form the scene presents as, e.g. rising.

shape.description: Data shape, e.g. series, groups, funnel.

archetype.description: Archetype, e.g. trend, where, flow, driver.

tools.name: get_canonical_forms
tools.description: The canonical form vocabulary — the structural primitive. 7 data shapes and the 33 canonical forms they resolve to. The form is why one engine reads compensation, attrition, funnels and survey data without a per-domain rewrite: the domain is in the metric tag, the structure is here. 'oftenMeans' is a labelled heuristic, never a conclusion.

tools.name: get_claim_warrant
tools.description: How many works discuss a claim — discourse volume, with the works named. For a construct pair mined from the book corpus: how many distinct works discuss the link, and which ones, with each work's stated rationale. ⚠ This is DISCOURSE, not evidence — book frequency is confounded by publication incentives, fashion and citation cascades, so it is reported as 'discussed in N works' and never as corroboration, confidence, or a score. Single-work claims are returned, labelled as such; corroboration is not a gate. No query returns corpus-level stats including a counting discrepancy we state openly.

from.description: Source construct, e.g. employee_engagement. Use with `to`.

to.description: Target construct, e.g. employee_turnover. Use with `from`.

construct.description: Every pair the corpus links this construct to, most-discussed first.

focus.description: Discourse volume for one focus area.

tools.name: get_library_ids
tools.description: Library id export — stable ids for the works homed here. Batch export of library_id rows (id, title, author, year, property tags) for the works that home on peopleanalyst.com. Ids are content-addressed (SHA-256 of normalized title|authors|year) and stable across repos, so a consumer can join to this catalog without string matching. Scoped to works homed here — titles whose canonical home is another property are excluded, matching /library.

tag.description: Filter by property tag, e.g. principia.

limit.description: Cap the number of rows returned.

tools.name: run_segmentation
tools.description: Behavioral segmentation, role discovery, and exemplar matching. Deterministic segmentation over caller-supplied numeric vectors: cluster subjects, discover roles from behaviour + relationship edges, detect emergent roles, or match against exemplars. Structured non-biometric signals only — no audio, video, or affect inference. The caller supplies all data; nothing is retained. Capped at 5,000 rows per request.

body.description: JSON request body accepted by the underlying endpoint.

tools.name: plan_next_data_ask
tools.description: What data to ask for next, and what it would rule out. The acquisition planner. Given which data-stories are still candidates, returns the single most efficient next question, the full ranked list, and the minimum set of asks that makes every live story testable — split into what can be sent today versus what needs legal review. Ranked by information-per-friction: how evenly an answer splits the live hypothesis set (computed by entropy from the discrimination matrix, never hand-asserted) divided by a cost in which GOVERNANCE outweighs effort. Absent priors all live stories weigh equally, so results reflect structure, not likelihood. GET accepts ?live=, ?have=, ?lack= as comma lists.

body.description: JSON request body accepted by the underlying endpoint.

tools.name: get_insight_cards
tools.description: A pitch rendered as player-ready InsightCards. Serves a named pitch as an ordered InsightCard[] (the cross-site insight-player contract). ?pitch selects the pitch; ?awareness optionally reshapes the sequence for the buyer's awareness state.

awareness.description: Awareness state to reshape the sequence.

tools.name: get_situations
tools.description: Demonstration scenarios (discovered → diagnosed → solved). The proof layer paired with brandscripts: concrete situations a product resolves. ?product filters; ?status opts into drafts.

tools.name: get_tools
tools.description: The PeopleAnalyst tool catalog (corpus-grounded acting tools). Machine-readable catalog of every corpus-grounded acting tool — name, category, what it does, inputs/outputs, concrete use cases, the profile URL, and how to run it (auth-gated REST + MCP). Last production probe (2026-09-23) reported grounded: true. Discovery is open (find + cite the tools); execution is API-key gated. ?category filters by family; ?slug returns one tool.

category.description: Filter by family (e.g. Marketing, Startup & strategy, Software engineering).

slug.description: Return a single tool by slug (e.g. positioning).
